problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=6-2t,$ where $t⩾0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s},$ calculate the maximum velocity ${v}_{\text{max}}$ of the particle and determine the time when the particle reaches its maximum velocity.

activity_context.topic_title: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Integration

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2-\frac{2}{3}t,$ where $t⩾0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=4\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s},$ calculate the maximum velocity ${v}_{\text{max}}$ of the particle and determine the time when the particle reaches its maximum velocity.
feedback.worked_solution:
The extrema of the velocity $v$ occur at the critical points of $v.$

Since $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=a(t),$ to find the times where $v$ is a maximum, we just need to solve $a(t)=0$ and test each solution using the first or second derivative test.

Solving $a(t)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =0 \\ 2-\frac{2}{3}t & =0 \\ t & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the extremum of the velocity function occurs when $t=3\,\text{s}.$

We now test the extreme value using the second derivative test. For this, we find the second derivative of $v(t)$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}v}{\text{d}{t}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(a(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-\frac{2}{3}t) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${v}^{″}(3)<0,$ we conclude that the velocity is maximized when $t=3\,\text{s}.$

Now, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2-\frac{2}{3}t)\text{d}t \\  & =2t-\frac{1}{3}{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2(0)-\frac{1}{3}(0)^{2}+C & =4 \\ 0+0+C & =4\,⟹\,C=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2t-\frac{1}{3}{t}^{2}+4.$

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

$$
{v}_{\text{max}}=v(3)=2(3)-\frac{1}{3}(3)^{2}+4=7\,\text{m}/\text{s}
$$
